hints: Focus on how the carbonyl group in propanal is polarised, and think about what type of reagent would be attracted to the slightly positive carbon.
Look at the product $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$ and count how many different groups are attached to the carbon bearing the OH group.
Remember the difference between a nucleophile and an electrophile, then decide whether a negative $\text{CN}^-$ ion would donate or accept an electron pair.
walkthrough:
**Recall the nucleophilic addition mechanism**

Think of the C=O bond as polarised, with carbon $\delta+$ and oxygen $\delta-$. The negative cyanide ion is attracted to that $\delta+$ carbon.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(O}^-\text{)CN}$$

**Check statement 1**

That first attack by $\text{CN}^-$ forms an alkoxide intermediate ion, which is later protonated by HCN to give the cyanohydrin and regenerate $\text{CN}^-$. So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 for chirality**

Look at the product carbon in $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$. It is bonded to four different groups: H, OH, CN and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

A carbon with four different groups is chiral, so statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3, nucleophile versus electrophile**

A nucleophile donates an electron pair, an electrophile accepts an electron pair. $\text{CN}^-$ has a lone pair and a negative charge, so it is a strong nucleophile, not an electrophile.

Statement 3 reverses the roles, so it is incorrect. With 1 and 2 correct only, we select that combination.

options.A: This option claims statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 1 and 2 are true, but statement 3 is false because $\text{CN}^-$ is a nucleophile, not an electrophile.
options.B: This option claims only 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 1 is true from nucleophilic attack to give the alkoxide intermediate. Statement 2 is true because the product carbon attached to OH, H, CN and ethyl is chiral.
options.C: This option claims only 2 and 3 are correct. It correctly includes 2 but wrongly includes 3 and wrongly leaves out 1. $\text{CN}^-$ is the nucleophile that starts the mechanism, so 1 must be included.
options.D: This option claims only 1 is correct. It correctly includes 1 but wrongly leaves out 2. The product $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$ clearly has a carbon with four different substituents, so it is chiral.
